caption:
Yes, bookkeeping is “boring.” 
I’ll say it first. 😅

But here’s what most people miss.

That unglamorous, 
behind-the-scenes work is one of the most flexible, 
location-independent, 
life-giving businesses you can build, if you build it right.

And the best part?
Anyone can do this.✨

And the bookkeepers that have aren’t “better” then you.

They’ve just built their business with the right pricing, the right systems, and the right boundaries so it funds the life instead of swallowing it whole.

That’s the difference between a business that keeps you glued to your desk and one that gives you the freedom, income, and flexibility you started this for in the first place.

And that’s exactly what I help bookkeepers do: turn a good little bookkeeping business into one that actually supports the life they want.

If that’s the business you’re ready to build, you’re in the right place. 🤍

Comment or DM me COLLECTIVE and let’s talk about what’s possible for you.

#bookkeepingcoach #bookkeepingcommunity #bookkeeperlife

“I’m just a bookkeeper.” 🛑 
Let’s retire that sentence for good.

Every time you add that little word “just” you shrink what you actually do. 

And here’s the thing: the way you talk about your work trains other people how to value it (and how to price it).

Because you’re not “just” anything. 

✨You catch the errors that save your clients thousands. 
✨You help them understand whether they can afford to hire, or grow, or take a paycheque. 
✨You give them peace of mind at tax time. 
✨You know their numbers better than they do.

That’s not data entry. 

That’s a financial partner, a problem solver, and a business owner all in one.

So drop the “just.” 

Not because it’s a cute mindset tweak, but because confidence in how you describe your work shows up everywhere:

⚡️your pricing
⚡️your marketing
⚡️your discovery calls
⚡️and the clients you attract. 🤍

Say it with me: I’m a bookkeeper. 
Full stop.

#bookkeepingcoach #bookkeepingcommunity #bookkeeperlife

caption:
There’s this belief in our industry that a client who’s been with you “since the beginning” has earned a permanent seat. 

That leaving would be disloyal, or ungrateful, or unkind. 

So we hold onto them long past the point where the relationship actually fits.

But here’s what I want you to sit with: you are not the same bookkeeper you were when you signed that client. 

Your rates have changed. 
Your skills have changed. 
Your standards, your capacity, and your idea of a dream client have all changed. 

And it is completely okay if a client from years ago doesn’t grow alongside all of that.

Holding on out of guilt doesn’t make you loyal, it just keeps you stuck. 

That client takes up a spot an aligned, better-fit client could fill. 

They take energy you could be pouring into the work you actually love. 

And more often than not, you start to feel it every time their name shows up in your inbox.

And this is the part people forget: staying isn’t automatically good for them either. 

Maybe a client has outgrown you (or never quite fit in the first place) and would be better served by someone whose business is built for exactly what they need right now.

So if you’ve been carrying one of these clients, know that you can make a change.

You’re allowed to outgrow clients. 
You’re allowed to build the roster you actually want. 

Curious if a client come to mind while reading this?

Knowing when (and how) to let a client go without the guilt is exactly the kind of thing we work through inside the Collective.

caption:
If you’re a bookkeeper, I’d bet you’ve done this without even noticing. 

Their late documents become your stress. 
Their missing receipts keep you up at night. 
Their “I forgot” turns into your weekend spent catching up.

And it makes sense.

You care, you’re good at your job, and you want to do right by people. 

But caring about your clients was never supposed to mean absorbing their chaos into your own body.

Their disorganization isn’t a reflection of your ability, and it isn’t yours to fix by sacrificing your own peace. 

You can hold clear boundaries, real deadlines, a plan for missed ones, honest communication about the impact, and still be a warm, generous bookkeeper. 

Those two things are not opposites.

Being organized and calm in your own business, even when your clients aren’t, isn’t cold or mean.

It’s putting yourself and your business first, and may be the only way to do this work long-term without running yourself into the ground.

caption:
Four years ago, I would have said yes to any client who wanted to work with me. 

The result? 

Months of stress, scope creep, underpricing and clients who saw me as cheap labor instead of a financial professional.

Now I know exactly what to listen for in those initial conversations, and more importantly, when to investigate further vs. when to run.

These red flags have saved me from so many headaches and helped me build a client roster full of people who actually value what our team does and that we have great relationships with.

Swipe through to read six red flags to look out for and if you should investigate or politely pass. 

Your gut is usually right about these things.
Trust it.

caption:
Don’t focus on the wrong activities! 👀

I’ve had the unique opportunity this year to work with over 200 bookkeepers on a 1:1 basis, with many of them starting from ground zero.

But one of the biggest mistakes I see them making is focusing on things that don’t matter in that phase of business.

Remember, every successful business out there has been built on a strong foundation.

And that is no different for your own business.

Without that solid foundation, you are going to struggle to see the results you’re looking for and goals you’re working towards.

And at the same time, I’ve gotten to work with bookkeepers looking to grow and expand their business.

But the same thing applies.

These business owners are focused on starting tasks, rather than activities that will fill their client roster, grow their income, their audience and their referrals.

Swipe through to see the key areas you need to focus on whether you’re starting or scaling your business ➡️

And if you’re ready to build a solid foundation for your business AND grow or EXPAND it in 2026/2027 - DM me COLLECTIVE and let’s get your name on the waitlist for our final round until 2028!

caption:
The hardest part isn’t knowing which workflows to document. 

It’s actually sitting down to do it. 😅

So here’s the method I teach 👇 the brain dump:

Open a doc and list your business “departments.” 

Even as a solo bookkeeper you have them: 
✨Marketing
✨Sales
✨Operations
✨Finance
✨HR

Under each one, write out every task you do, daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly. 

Don’t organize it, just dump it all out.

Then go back through and mark anything that feels repetitive, manual, or frustrating.

That list is your SOP to-do list, already in priority order.

Two things that make this actually work:
1. Document what you ALREADY do, not some perfect version you’ve never done. You can improve it once it exists on paper.
2. And don’t aim for perfect. A process that works 80% of the time and is written down will always beat a flawless one that only lives in your head.

And if you’re not even sure where your time is going right now? 

Track everything for one month first. 

The data will tell you exactly which workflow to build.

Which of the four are you starting with? 👇

(We build all of these out step by step inside the Collective, September is our final round until 2028. Link in bio for the waitlist 🤍)

It ended up being one of the busiest seasons I’ve had.

caption:
Let me say it a little louder for the bookkeepers hiding from their own content 👋

• You don’t need to go viral. 
• You don’t need a trending dance. 
• You don’t need to post five times a day or show your face to a million strangers.

Marketing your business isn’t about becoming an influencer, it’s about becoming visible to the right people.

✨It’s showing up consistently. 
✨Speaking directly to your ideal client’s problems. 
✨Sharing what you know, so that when someone’s finally ready to hire a bookkeeper, you’re the first person they think of.

That’s it. 

You’re building trust with your audience which is done one post at a time. 🤍

So if “I don’t want to be an influencer” has been your reason for staying invisible… consider this your permission slip to market in a way that actually feels like you.

And remember, the hardest part is getting started. 👀

So stop overthinking it and just post the content! 

The more you create, the easier it will become.

caption:
Here’s the thing nobody tells you when you’re starting out: the rate you set today was decided by a less experienced and confident version of you. 

And a lot of us set those early prices from a place of “please just say yes” instead of “this is what my work is worth.”

That’s not a mistake, it’s just where you started (and where a lot of bookkeepers start). 

The mistake is leaving those prices frozen while everything else about you grows.

Because your skills grow. 
Your speed grows. 
Your confidence grows. 
Your value to that client grows. 

But if the price never moves, you slowly end up doing your best work for your oldest, lowest number, while turning away the clients who’d happily pay what you’re worth now.

So here’s your permission slip: your prices are allowed to change as you do. 

Raising a rate isn’t greedy. 

It’s just keeping your business honest about who you’ve become.

A few signs it’s time to take a look: → You feel a little pang when their name pops up → You’ve raised your rates for new clients but not existing ones → You’d never quote that number today

caption:
As bookkeepers, we spend all year reminding our clients how essential financial clarity is..

Yet somehow we tend to skip that part in our own business when planning for the year ahead.

And as we move into 2026, this is the exact moment where most bookkeepers either set themselves up for a focused, profitable year, or end up repeating the same patterns that held them back in 2025.

Here’s the truth.
 You cannot create the lifestyle, schedule, or income you want in 2026 if you don’t know what you’re working toward or how your numbers support it.

I see so many bookkeepers absolutely crushing it with client work, but when it comes to their own financial goals? 

It’s a lot of guessing, hoping, and “I’ll figure it out later.”

Goal-setting isn’t busy work. 

It’s the foundation that informs how many clients you need, how you price, how you structure your time, and what your capacity actually looks like.

You started your business for a reason, maybe it’s more travel, more freedom, more financial stability, shorter workweeks, or the ability to build real savings.
 Whatever your goals are for 2026, they won’t happen by accident.
 But if your goals say one thing, but your pricing, systems, and capacity say something completely different, you’ll always feel behind. 

We need a vision to start the business and stay focused on growing it, but the math behind the vision also need to make sense.

This is why setting aligned sales and profit goals matters. 

When you know exactly what you want to earn, how much time you want to work, and the lifestyle you’re building toward, you can reverse-engineer the exact number of clients you need, and the gaps you need to close to get there.

In 2026, you don’t need more hustle.
 You need clarity, alignment, and a plan you can actually execute.

caption:
I’m sure you’ve seen “faceless” accounts all over IG.

They say that anyone can grow a successful business on social media and do so with never showing up on stories, posting photos of yourself and only using stock b-roll video.

And sure, they might work if you’re selling a digital product where the buyer doesn’t care who you are.

But bookkeeping? That’s different.

Finances = money.
Money = emotions

After 13+ years in this industry, I can tell you that most business owners have complicated relationships with their finances. They feel vulnerable, overwhelmed, sometimes even ashamed about the state of their books.

Your job as a bookkeeper isn’t just to reconcile accounts. It’s to support business owners in understanding their finances so they can make informed decisions.

That requires trust. And trust requires showing up as a real person.

If Instagram is your main platform for connecting with potential clients, but you’re not showing your face, you’re making it so much harder to build that know, like, and trust factor BEFORE they even get on a discovery call with you.

Think about it from your ideal client’s perspective:

Would YOU hire a bookkeeper who’s going to have insight into every detail of your business and finances—without even knowing what they look like or how they communicate?

Probably not. So why would your audience be any different?

This is what was happening with Collective member S. 

She was posting consistently but staying completely faceless. 

Once we shifted her strategy to actually show up: her face, her voice, her personality, everything changed.

caption:
You think you’re charging enough, but are you actually accounting for ALL the costs of running your business?

Here are the hidden expenses most bookkeepers forget to factor in:

✨Your time beyond the actual client work: 
👉Client communication, emails, discovery calls, follow-ups, project management, this easily adds 20-40% to your actual “bookkeeping” time.

✨Business overhead: 
👉Your software subscriptions, internet, phone, computer equipment, insurance, continuing education.

✨Taxes: 
👉As a business owner, you need to save for income taxes, and if you have payroll, the employer portion of what that costs. 

✨Your operational time: 
👉Marketing, admin work, invoicing, networking, business development (all essential but not directly billable hours)

✨Payment processing fees: 
👉Whether it’s Stripe, PayPal, or your bank, every payment has a cost.

✨The cost of your expertise: 
👉You’re not just entering numbers, you’re providing financial insights, catching errors, and giving business owners peace of mind.  
✨Seasonal fluctuations: 
👉Those slower months need to be supported by the busier ones.

✨Growth investments: 
👉Training, courses, coaching and tools to improve your business

Most bookkeepers think about what they want to make per hour and forget about everything else.

The result? 

Working harder for less money and wondering why their business isn’t more profitable.

Your rates should include everything: your expertise, your overhead, your taxes, your unbillable time, 

AND a profit margin for growth.

When you factor in all these hidden costs, that hourly price you thought was good now needs to be doubled or even tripled to create a profit.

Take a hard look at your pricing and ask yourself if you’re covering ALL your costs, or just hoping it works out?

caption:
It’s not about filling your roster with low-paying clients or working 60-hour weeks.

Here’s what actually going to help you get to $5K and $10k months:

1. Price based on your profit goals, not what feels comfortable 
Stop undercharging because you’re worried about what people will think. 

Do the math: what do you need to charge per client to hit your revenue goals without burning out? 

Price for the business you want to build, not the one you think you deserve right now.

2. Create a solid base package and build from there 
Start with one strong monthly bookkeeping package that covers your core services. 

Then customize by adding on based on what each client actually needs. 

This keeps your process consistent across clients, reduces decision fatigue, and makes onboarding so much easier, while still feeling tailored to each business.

3. Master your discovery call process 
Most bookkeepers lose clients before they even send a proposal. 

Your discovery call isn’t just about gathering information, it’s about building trust, uncovering their real problems, and positioning yourself as the solution.

4. Have real systems for onboarding 
If every new client feels like you’re starting from scratch, you’ll burn out before you hit $5K. 

Welcome guides, document collection processes, and onboarding workflows save you hours and make clients feel taken care of.

5. Market consistently (not just when you need clients)
The bookkeepers hitting $5K months aren’t posting once a week when they remember. 

They show up consistently, share their expertise, and build trust BEFORE people need a bookkeeper.

6. Set boundaries from day one 
Scope creep, late-night texts, and clients who don’t respect your process will kill your profitability. Setting professional boundaries isn’t optional, it’s what keeps your business sustainable.

Inside the Collective, we cover all of this, discovery calls, pricing strategies, onboarding systems, client management, marketing, and building a business that actually supports your life.

caption:
Luxury looks different for everyone. And honestly? That’s the whole point.

I’m always seeing those reels with the designer bags, the five-star hotels, the perfectly curated “rich life.” And if that’s what lights you up? 

Great! Build your business toward that! Zero judgment here.

But I didn’t start this business for any of that.

I started it for moments like deciding on a random Wednesday night to buy last-minute tickets to World Series Game 6 and 7 with my best friend. 

And then actually hopping on a plane the next morning because I could. ⚾️✈️

I built this for the freedom to surprise my husband with a two-week ski trip to Japan. 

To drive home last minute and show up at my niece and nephew’s door for Christmas. 

To tell our oldest niece “Pick anywhere in the world, we’re taking you on a graduation trip.”

To hop in the van and take off for a week because we felt like it.

The version of wealth I wanted was never about things. 

It was about time, flexibility, and saying yes to life when it calls.

Even when business is hard (and these last two months have been really hard), these moments remind me why I keep going. Why this is worth it a thousand times over.

My kind of luxury? It’s freedom. 

The kind you can’t put in a shopping bag or check into a hotel room.

When you’re building your business, or even figuring out what you want to do, I think it’s important to go inward. Get off socials, write out what YOU want. 

Maybe that’s a luxury bag or car, maybe its travel, maybe its your own home, more time in your schedule… but once you figured it out, it makes working hard toward it a lot easier.

caption:
Stop doing this 👇🏻

OVERTHINKING!!

I cannot tell you how much TIME and ENERGY I wasted overthinking everything!! 

👉🏻 My business name
👉🏻 My branding colors
👉🏻 My website
👉🏻 What my processes should look like
👉🏻 What questions my clients were going to ask and if I would know the answer
👉🏻 And so much more!

Overthinking stopped me from actually taking ACTION, launching my business and getting started.

Yes there are some things you are going to want to think about before you start offering your services like 
✨ What services do I want to offer?
✨ What do I want my pricing to look like?
✨ What accounting software am I going to use?

But even if you have everything figured out, I can tell you that things WILL change.

Because that’s how business goes. 🤷‍♀️

ESPECIALLY when you are just getting it off the ground. 

You will figure out what works best for you and your business, but the only way you are going to actually do that is by taking the first step.

Overthinking, going back on forth on decisions, changing your mind on things…

None of that is helpful or makes any difference if you haven’t brought on any clients or started marketing your services.

You can be the most technically skilled bookkeeper in the world and still burn out, lose money, and resent your clients, all because you never set boundaries.

Knowing how to say 
•”I don’t work weekends”
•”That’s outside our scope”

Technical skills get you hired. Boundaries keep you in business.

caption:
This is our fourth year of taking a two week holiday break at Enroute🎄

Before we dive into how we prepare for our breaks, what does a two week holiday break actually look like for our team of five. 

For Enroute, that means our bookkeepers are fully off during this time. 

They aren’t expected (and are also encouraged not to) check their emails, respond to client inquiries, do any client work, check in with me for deadlines, think or worry about work in any capacity. 

I truly value my team and fully want them to take this time off and enjoy it with their family and friends. 

For me, taking a two week holiday looks like everything from above, with the exception of any specific deadline tasks that happen during our scheduled holiday break.

Now, you might be reading this thinking, “two weeks isn’t that long of a break, why are you even worried?”

I get that it might not seem like a long time to some people, but as a business owner (especially if you’re a solo practice), taking two weeks fully off your business can feel a little overwhelming.

But I promise as someone who has been through it, it’s really not that bad, and the great thing about bookkeeping is there really isn’t ever any 911 situations, so don’t stress about it too much. 

Remember, at the end of the day, you’re human and you have a life outside your business, just like your clients, so as long as you do the best, are transparent with your clients, if anything does go sideways you can always learn and make improvements for next time. 

Swipe through the slides to see the steps we take to prep and plan for our two week break.

caption:
It can be hard working from home, being your own boss and wanting to make sure your clients feel fully supported at all times. 

You see an email pop up during the day, at night or on the weekend and think “oh I can quickly answer this, that’s no problem!”.   But what you’re doing is stopping the current task you’re working on, switching your attention to this email, and then trying to go back to that previous task. 

Although it might seem like it doesn’t disrupt your day, switching between tasks lowers your productivity and makes it harder for you to get into that deep focus and flow state while working. 

On the other hand, if your client expects you to respond right away, then we need to focus our attention on your boundaries. 

Boundaries and expectations around communication should be set from day one when the client reaches out and should be discussed during onboarding and outlined on your contracts. 

This could include:
📧 Clearly outlining what your response time will be (within 24 hours, 48, 3 business days, etc)
📲 Letting your clients know how you will communicate with them (email, messaging app, etc)
📅 Stating your working days (ex. Mon to Thu 9-4)

Even if you decide to work outside of your “working hours”, use the scheduled send feature on your email to continue to reinforce those boundaries. 

Internally to help that compulsion of answering right away, you can turn off email notifications on your computer, sign out of your work email on days off or use a phone app so that you can send calls and texts directly to voicemail until you’re back at work. 

If you’re reading this thinking, “oh shit - I need to fix this”, don’t worry it’s not too late. 

I recommend sending out an email to your clients to reset expectations around communication so that you are both on the same page about what that looks like.  

And remember, the great thing about bookkeeping is there are few emergencies that require an immediate response, so you can use this to your advantage to set up a schedule and workflow that fits best for you and your life.

You think you’re charging enough, but are you actually accounting for ALL the costs of running your business?

Here are the hidden expenses most bookkeepers forget to factor in:

✨Your time beyond the actual client work: 
👉Client communication, emails, discovery calls, follow-ups, project management, this easily adds 20-40% to your actual “bookkeeping” time.

✨Business overhead: 
👉Your software subscriptions, internet, phone, computer equipment, insurance, continuing education.

✨Taxes: 
👉As a business owner, you need to save for income taxes, and if you have payroll, the employer portion of what that costs. 

✨Your operational time: 
👉Marketing, admin work, invoicing, networking, business development (all essential but not directly billable hours)

✨Payment processing fees: 
👉Whether it’s Stripe, PayPal, or your bank, every payment has a cost.

✨The cost of your expertise: 
👉You’re not just entering numbers, you’re providing financial insights, catching errors, and giving business owners peace of mind.  
✨Seasonal fluctuations: 
👉Those slower months need to be supported by the busier ones.

✨Growth investments: 
👉Training, courses, coaching and tools to improve your business

Most bookkeepers think about what they want to make per hour and forget about everything else.

Your business will only be as strong as the conversations you’re willing to have.

caption:
What is one thing that MOST new bookkeepers struggle with when they start offering their services?

CONFIDENCE! 

I can remember starting my first job as a bookkeeper having NO idea what I was doing, thinking “it’ll be okay, I’m sure I’ll do training first!”. 

Little did I know that since my job was at a fairly new start-up there was no training program in place. 😲

Shocked was an understatement.

Instead it was more “here’s your team, here’s your clients, good luck!”.

It was TERRIFYING!

Luckily I had such a great manager who did an excellent job at training, answering questions and correcting my mistakes. 

But what I really could have used during that time was PRACTICE!

Which is why in the Academy, I’ve created a full Mock Client library that does EXACTLY that!

I want you to be able to walk away feeling confident in not only your understanding of bookkeeping, what you need to do and why, but also your skills and abilities and at the same time exposing you to the reality of what it’s like working with real clients.

So what are our mock clients?

These are full clients that act exactly as clients would in the real world. 
You download a file that comes with their transactions, statements, and everything else that you need to complete their books. 

From there you go through all of the steps from setting them up in QBO, to entering transactions, working through specific problems and issues, reconciling the accounts and reviewing the financial statements.

caption:
Pricing has to be one of the most common issues that I see with new bookkeepers.

“How much should I charge?”
“What am I charging for?”
“Should I charge hourly or fixed?”
“How do I figure out what to charge?”

And the list goes on.

Now pricing is one of those things in bookkeeping where “it depends” (the worst I know).

It depends on your experience, the client’s you’re working with, what your niche is, if you’re a solo business owner or if you have a team, what your goals are, what services you offer and more.

But there is one thing when it comes to pricing that if you’ve followed me even for just a few months you will know how I feel about it… and that’s hourly pricing.

As tempting as it might be, especially if you’re a new bookkeeper, I do not recommend that you charge your services on an hourly basis.

Fixed fee or value based pricing are way better options that will help increase your profit as your business grows and as you become more experienced and a better bookkeeper.

Swipe through to read just a few of the reasons why I think hourly pricing hurts not only your businesses bottom line, but is also a worse option for your client as well.

Now there will be moments when pricing hourly might be your best option.

Maybe you have a one-off project with a client that makes more sense doing hourly.

Or maybe a new client isn’t able to give you enough information to price accurately so hourly for the first month or two is the best option until you get a better sense of what’s happening.

But for your regular monthly bookkeeping clients, I would try to stay away from charging hourly.

If you have any questions around charging a fixed fee or value based pricing, leave them in the comments below, or DM me and let’s chat. ✨

Do you charge hourly fixed or another way?

caption:
Hi - I’m Stacie :) 

I started my bookkeeping business, Enroute Accounting, in 2021 after feeling completely unmotivated and unsatisfied at my 9–5.

After I quit, I was convinced I was done with bookkeeping forever. I spent months debating what to do next—going back to school, getting a random job in my small town, anything that didn’t involve the word “bookkeeping.”

But after awhile I realized it wasn’t bookkeeping I hated—it was being told how to work. The set hours, have to request time off, the income cap, and taking on twice the work for a tiny raise.

I actually enjoyed the work and realized I could take my skills and build something that worked on my terms.

Was it terrifying? 100%. Did I think it would work? Honestly, no clue. 
But after I made the decision to go for it I was 120% committed to showing up each and every day until it did.

And it did.

Three months in, I almost quit because things were so slow—but thanks to my best friend’s encouragement, I kept going. 

Soon after, things started to snowball.
✨ Seven months in, I hit $10k in MRR. 
✨ Three years later, we’ve crossed $650k in revenue, have a team of four amazing bookkeepers, and bring increased our MRR to over $25k.

The biggest win? The flexibility, freedom, and life I’ve been able to build along the way: 
✨ Paying off $40k in debt 
✨ Traveling to Europe (twice!) and New Zealand for a month 
✨ Taking my sisters on an all-paid trip to Italy 
✨ Surprising my husband with his dream trip to Iceland 
✨ Converting a sprinter van to travel even more

I’m not sharing this to brag, but to show you what’s possible.

I’m not special or different. 

I started making $40k/year in a job I didn’t love. But I made the decision to change, believed in myself, and, most importantly, took action and stayed committed even when it got hard.

It’s been 1130 days since I started Enroute, and my life has completely changed.

If you’re ready to change yours, know this: you CAN do it too. 

Use my story and the story of so many Collective members as proof that your bookkeeping business can fund your dreams, passions, and give you the life you’ve always wanted. 💫

caption:
This is our third year of taking a two week holiday break at Enroute🎄

Before we dive into how we prepare for our breaks, what does a two week holiday break actually look like for our team of five. 

For Enroute, that means our bookkeepers are fully off during this time. 

They aren’t expected (and are also encouraged not to) check their emails, respond to client inquiries, do any client work, check in with me for deadlines, think or worry about work in any capacity. 

I truly value my team and fully want them to take this time off and enjoy it with their family and friends. 

For me, taking a two week holiday looks like everything from above, with the exception of any specific deadline tasks that happen during our scheduled holiday break (I go more into detail on this for #3 check for deadlines).

Now, you might be reading this thinking, “two weeks isn’t that long of a break, why are you even worried?”

I get that it might not seem like a long time to some people, but as a business owner (especially if you’re a solo practice), taking two weeks fully off your business can feel a little overwhelming.

But I promise as someone who has been through it, it’s really not that bad, and the great thing about bookkeeping is there really isn’t ever any 911 situations, so don’t stress about it too much. 

Remember, at the end of the day, you’re human and you have a life outside your business, just like your clients, so as long as you do the best, are transparent with your clients, if anything does go sideways you can always learn and make improvements for next time. 

Swipe through the slides to see the steps we take to prep and plan for our two week break. 

And if you have any questions pop them into the comments below 👇🏻

I wanted a job where I could work from wherever I wanted, make as much money as I wanted, have little client-facing responsibility and above all, I wanted to work with clients I actually liked.

I can tell you without a doubt that if you want a job that gives you all the flexibility, freedom and income you desire, bookkeeping is where you need to be. 

Heck, as I post this I’m currently figuring out where we’re taking the van next year on our month long trips, all without having to worry about asking for time off or how I was going to afford it. 🚐

I was a bookkeeper BEFORE I started my own business and would have never even thought this was a possibility just over three years ago.🤯

caption:
I’m sure you’ve seen “faceless” accounts all over IG this year.

They say that anyone can grow a successful business and do so with never showing up on stories, posting photos of yourself and only using stock b-roll video.

And while that might work if you sell a digital product where the buyer doesn’t care who you are, as a bookkeeper, this just isn’t going to work. 

Bookkeeping is a job centred around finances

Finances = money.
Money = emotions

After being in the industry for over 12 years I can tell you that a lot of business owners have deeply rooted money mindset issues, or can feel weird or uncomfortable when it comes to learning, talking and sharing about their finances. 

As a bookkeeper, your job is to support business owners in not only keeping their books up to date, but understanding what’s happening with their finances so they can take that information and make informed business decisions.

This takes building a trusting relationship with your clients which is why long-term client retention is so important - but that’s a post for another day. 

So if you’ve said that IG is going to be THE main platform you use to market your business and connect with potential clients, but you’re NOT showing your face, you’re doing a huge disservice to your business. 

How are business owners going to build that like, know and trust with you BEFORE getting on a discovery call if all you post is graphics, never talk on stories, or even have no photos of yourself on your website?

This is what was happening with Collective member S. Swipe —> to read about the changes we made and how that transformed her business.

Put yourself in your audience’s shoes.

Would you hire a bookkeeper that is going to have insight into every single detail of your business and finances without even knowing what they look like?

Is your answer no? If it is, why would it be any different for your audience?

If you’re struggling using social media to build that know, like and trust with your audience so that they CHOOSE you to be their bookkeeper - then you need to be inside the Collective.

Our biggest event is happening in 5 days… see you there! 🔥

caption:
Pricing has to be one of the most common issues that I see with new bookkeepers.

“How much should I charge?”
“What am I charging for?”
“Should I charge hourly or fixed?”
“How do I figure out what to charge?”

And the list goes on.

Now pricing is one of those things in bookkeeping where “it depends” (the worst I know).

It depends on your experience, the client’s you’re working with, what your niche is, if you’re a solo business owner or if you have a team, what your goals are, what services you offer and more.

But there is one thing when it comes to pricing that if you’ve followed me even for just a few months you will know how I feel about it… and that’s hourly pricing.

As tempting as it might be, especially if you’re a new bookkeeper, I do not recommend that you charge your services on an hourly basis.

Fixed fee or value based pricing are way better options that will help increase your profit as your business grows and as you become more experienced and a better bookkeeper.

Swipe through to read just a few of the reasons why I think hourly pricing hurts not only your businesses bottom line, but is also a worse option for your client as well.

Now there will be moments when pricing hourly might be your best option.

Maybe you have a one-off project with a client that makes more sense doing hourly.

Or maybe a new client isn’t able to give you enough information to price accurately so hourly for the first month or two is the best option until you get a better sense of what’s happening.

But for your regular monthly bookkeeping clients, I would try to stay away from charging hourly.

Pricing is a big focus for a lot of the Collective members and it should be because it can be the make or break of your business. Inside the program we work 1:1 to ensure your pricing and packages are set up in a way that suite your ideal client, your business and long term goals/growth.

caption:
If you’re scrolling on the ‘gram right now, there’s a good chance you’re seeing...

💸 Someone celebrating hitting their big six-figure revenue goal
💸 Another person quitting their full-time job to travel
💸 Someone else booking DREAM clients left and right

But here’s the reality: You will NEVER see the full picture on Instagram. Most people WON’T show you:

➖ The EXHAUSTING 16-hour days they put in
➖ The MONTHS of crickets in the DMs despite posting every day
➖ The imposter syndrome and fear around success

When I first started my bookkeeping business, I remember voice messaging my friend and saying, “I’m going to give myself until the end of February. If it doesn’t work by then, I’ll try something else.”

This is after I had been doing ALL the things:

➖ Networking with people IRL and online
➖ Providing SO much free value on Instagram and posting once or twice a day, knowing I was talking to less than 100 people (most of which were family and friends)
➖ Investing in mentorships, training, and using free resources when I couldn’t afford paid options

And my friend did something incredible. She hit me with a MAJOR truth bomb that I needed to hear:

“Stacie, it’s only been a few months! Everything you’ve been doing will snowball before you know it.”

And just three weeks later...That’s EXACTLY what happened!

I decided to work the things I COULD control, not wait around for clients to fall in my lap. But I HAD to be okay with being in the trenches for a minute.

If you’re there right now, you are NOT alone. 
It took me FOUR months to see any movement in my business. But I was consistent through it all - and that’s what I attribute to being where I am today.

You can get there on your own - I know you can. But what if there was a way to fast-track your growth and avoid the common pitfalls most business owners will make the first time around?

That’s exactly why I started the Virtual Bookkeeper’s Collective - a tailored mentorship program and community for new-to-business bookkeepers ready to build the sustainable business of their dreams. 
Spots are filling for 2025. DM me the word WAITLIST to get on the late list for early access and exclusive bonuses ✨

It’s time to give up the pen and paper.

We live in a time where you can hit one button and have a face to face video chat with your friend that lives on the other side of the world.

Yet here you are still manually writing down every task that needs to be completed for your clients in your notebook.

I’m sorry to break the news to you but this just isn’t good enough.

You’re a CEO that is trying to scale your bookkeeping business and bring on more clients every single month, and that means making smart choices that are going to aid you in doing that, not make it harder.

At this stage of the game, you need to have an online project management system.

Whether that’s Asana, Clickup, Trello, Notion.. It doesn’t matter as long as you’re using it. 

Because let’s face it, even if you’re attached to that scrappy notebook, it’s the least time efficient way of recording your task list each month and you have a high risk of missing or forgetting about tasks.

A project management system will be a game-changer for your business.

Once you have it set up, you’ll have all your client’s tasks, deadlines, and details in one place.

This makes it SO easy to see what tasks need to be completed each week, allowing you to better schedule your time. 

It’s also helpful for knowing where SOP’s need to be created in your business which makes it even easier for you if you ever want to bring on a team member or VA in the future.

Switching to a project management system will also give you back hours into your business that could be used to bring on a new client, increasing your monthly revenue and profit. 

And if you’re still feeling attached to your pen and paper, you can still use that throughout the week for quick notes here or there, but I recommend adding a reminder into your calendar once a week to move those notes from your paper, into your online system. 

If you’re ready to start implementing systems that are going to increase your profits and reduce the time spent in your business, I have something big coming for you next week.

caption:
I created a 6 figure bookkeeping business that allows me to work part time AND take a month long European vacation in a few weeks.⁠
⁠
But that didn’t “just happen”, it was a culture that I cultivated.⁠
⁠
So if your goal is to have a business that revolves around your life, not the other way around - bookkeeping is one of the only business models I know that can make that happen, and here’s why:⁠
⁠
🔥 Minimal client communication needed ⁠
⁠
I almost never have to ask my clients for information because their bookkeeping platforms house all the info I need - they know exactly what they need to upload on a monthly basis...⁠
⁠
Then if I do have to request documents - it’s a streamlined communication process! ⁠
⁠
So all I have to do to serve my clients is login, complete the work, pull the reports, analyze them, and have a call with my clients to go over them. ⁠
⁠
It eliminates so much of the daily communication and back and forth that so many other service providers experience in their roles and gives me so much freedom in my life. ⁠
⁠
🔥 Services are provided during one period of time in the month, not on a daily basis⁠
⁠
I balance my clients books on a MONTHLY basis so typically all client work is done at the end of the month, which gives me so much freedom during the rest of the month for other projects, travel, or for me to do whatever I want personally. ⁠
⁠
Again, we’re putting our lives first and THEN our businesses. ⁠
⁠
🔥 Role rapport and respect ⁠
⁠
It can be hard to find a good bookkeeper who actually gets their clients incredible results, treats them well, communicates, etc. ⁠
⁠
My clients respect me, and know I have their back, so they never micromanage or nitpick. ⁠
⁠
All of this creates a stress-free environment where I LOVE to serve my clients instead of dreading it, and have the freedom to make my life look however I want, while also making 6 figures. ⁠
⁠
Know you want to scale your bookkeeping business so you can live the life you quit your 9-5 for? ⁠
⁠

I wasted SO MUCH time! 😮‍💨

When I first started my business I stressed over my website.

I thought if I didn’t have the perfect, most beautiful *trendy* look, I’d never sign any clients.

And now looking back I know how ridiculous that is and how far from the truth it could be.

What was the point of having this website if there was no traffic going to it?

It was like planning the perfect road trip, mapping out all the stops and THEN remembering that you don’t even have a car.

I spent so much time that could have been put into social media, creating content and my marketing strategy… things that were ACTUALLY going to get my business in front of my ideal client’s eyes.

I know bookkeepers who have FULL client rosters, team members, a thriving business, and the closest thing they have to a website is their client interest form in Dubsado.

Don’t get me wrong, if you want to create a website - that’s great!

But it shouldn’t be your focus until you KNOW that you’re going to have people visiting it every day. 

If you’re not sure where to start when it comes to getting visibility in your business, something exciting is happening next week. 

The countdown is on.
8 days to go…. 🔥

caption:
When I tell you guys that bookkeeping is one of the easiest businesses to grow, I mean it.

I brought on my first five clients within a month of starting my business...

And brought on my NEXT five clients effortlessly within the next few months.

Then shortly after that I matched (and then exceeded) my corporate salary 🔥

The first five clients I brought on were a part of my personal network.

Now, most business owners can do their own marketing, sales, etc...

But one thing most businesses can’t do on their own (because they don’t understand it or just really don’t want to deal with it) is their books...

AND analyzing their own financial data to make informed, smart financial decisions.

So finding clients in this industry has NEVER been & never will be an issue.

But when I decided to start bringing on new clients, I turned to marketing myself.

I created a small but mighty audience on Instagram and made my services irresistible.

I made sure it was clear why I was unique as a bookkeeper & the value/ROI I’d bring to their business.

And because I didn’t want to constantly market myself...

I created a referral program for my clients so they got a kickback any time one of their referrals signed with me.

Having a strategy to sign your first several clients is ESSENTIAL to the success of your business...

BUT the cool part about bookkeeping is that in terms of signing clients, it’s a VERY easy business to do so for.

So if you’re sitting there thinking “how can I get my first client?!”, use these tools and remember you need to take ACTION on them. 

And if you’re wanting full support while starting your bookkeeping business, we have a few limited spots available in the Collective.

caption:
What’s the point of working with someone who doesn’t even try to get to know you?

I don’t believe in compartmentalizing your life into “business owner hat,” “bookkeeper hat,” and “person hat.” 

What’s happening in your personal life is going to affect your business, and your business should be designed to support your life—not the other way around.

When you join the Collective, you’re not just signing up for strategies and lessons—you’re gaining a coach who cares about you, not just as a bookkeeper or business owner, but as a person.

Here’s the thing: I’m not here to just help you grow your business. 

I’m here to support YOU—your growth as a bookkeeper, a CEO, and as a whole person. 

And I’ll be with you every step of the way.

In the coaching world, you’ll often hear that you should hold boundaries with clients, not get too close, and stay “friendly but professional.” 

You know what? Screw that.

Yes, I have boundaries with my clients—but when you hire me, you’re hiring me for a reason. 

I’m here to support you through everything you’re going through as a business owner.

I don’t just want to hear about your business wins and struggles. 

I want to hear about your weekend, your kid’s birthday party, the trip you’re planning, the thing you’re really stressed about right now, or the exciting milestone you just hit in your personal life.

Because how can I help you build a business that fits your vision and your lifestyle if I don’t even take the time to understand who YOU are?

This is why the Collective isn’t just another program. 
It’s a community and a partnership. 

Your success matters to me—and not just on paper, but in every part of your life. 🤍
